title: Corpus integrity
description: The integrity blob of CorpusProcess.wit, written from the server's own account of the run: what the results rest on and everything that did not go the plain way. sampling and rounds: the share of the packages the run asked to run on two machines and what came back of it, in a word and in a sentence, and for each round the packages that went out and the answers that came back, so that a run whose checking did not happen says so. pairs: the shards that came back twice, in the first round (the share CorpusOptions.SamplingRate asks for) or in the repair round (every shard of it, when the run asked for sampling), their two results compared on everything an honest node cannot vary (verdict, content hash, the hash of the signatures, document counts, drop and language histograms, the PDF counts). disputes: the shards whose copies disagreed, what up to three machines returned for each, and how each ended (outcome). no_result: the shards no machine returned an acceptable result for. rejected: the values dropped, by reason. A shard in none of these was run once and its result is one machine's word (single_execution). The platform keeps the copies of a shard on different machines and the document does not say which. The server sees values, not machines: in the first round and the repair round more values under a ticket than the round sent out are a dispute, in the dispute round they settle nothing, and there a value counts towards two machines only as far as it cannot be the second answer of a machine that left another package of the round short (outcome surplus_copies; a package is one shard in a job of up to 1,024 shards). Counting values as machines rests on the platform: Grid 1.3.0 and later keep, of what a node's batch returns, one value at most for each return variable its tasks asked for. With an older Grid a node could return several values for one task and this ruling would count them as machines. Version 8: version 7 with the second dispute round: a dispute the dispute round left with too few copies, or with a lead that may be one machine's second answers, goes out once more on three machines (again in its record, disputes_again and disputes_again_resolved in the summary, dispute_again in rounds), and a value under no ticket of the round no longer counts as a second answer one machine may have given. Version 7: version 6 with sampling and rounds, the repair round's pairs beside the first round's (round in every pair; repair_pairs, repair_compared and repair_mismatches in the summary) and repair_copies in a dispute's record: a shard that goes out again goes out on two machines when the run asked for sampling, and is ruled as a sampled shard of the first round is (up to version 6 it went to one machine, and two values under its ticket left it without a result). Version 6: the shape of version 5; tasks and results travel in packages, so a node that could not answer a package as a whole returns every shard of it as a fault (one more fault code, tasks: its task package did not arrive), and surplus also counts an answer beyond the ones a round opens for a package and two results for one shard in one answer. Version 5: version 4 let a result opt out of the comparison by the version it claimed, and chose the execution that stood for a shard by its own content hash.

controller.description: The server's controller version: the only one a result of this run carries.

single_execution.description: Shards whose accepted result is one machine's word: nothing compared it.

sampled.description: Shards that came back more than once in the first round (the pairs whose round is first). This and the six counters after it are of the first round: the run's sample.

compared.description: Pairs of the first round whose two sides are results with a verdict on the shard.

version_skew.description: Always 0; kept for readers of version 4. A result that claims another controller version is dropped and counted in rejected (reason version).

incomplete.description: Pairs with a side that is no result: a node fault or a dropped value (not compared; a mismatch is two results that disagree).

mismatches.description: Compared pairs that disagree; each is a dispute.

mismatch_rate.description: mismatches / compared; 0 when nothing was compared.

signatures_compared.description: Compared pairs whose sides made signatures, compared by their hashes (0 when the pipeline does not sign).

signature_mismatches.description: Compared pairs whose signatures differ (each also counted in mismatches, with signatures among its differences).

rejected_results.description: Values dropped over every round; rejected has them by reason.

node_faults.description: Results returned as a fault of the node, over every round (not the ones dropped as surplus).

repairs.description: Shards sent out once more: the first round left them without a result. On two machines when the run asked for sampling, on one otherwise.

repaired.description: Of those, the ones the second try gave a result (without a dispute).

repair_pairs.description: Shards that came back more than once in the repair round (the pairs whose round is repair).

repair_compared.description: Of those, the pairs whose two sides are results with a verdict on the shard.

repair_mismatches.description: Compared pairs of the repair round that disagree; each is a dispute. They are not in mismatch_rate: the shards of the repair round are no sample of the run.

no_result.description: Shards that ended without a result (NoResult in the report).

disputes.description: Shards whose copies disagreed, or that came back more often than they were sent out, in the first round or in the repair round.

disputes_resolved.description: Of those, the ones settled by the most machines, two at least, without a tie.

disputed.description: Of those, the ones that stayed open (Disputed in the report): out of the counts and the products.

disputes_again.description: Of the disputes, the ones that went out once more: the dispute round left them with too few copies, or with a lead that may be one machine's second answers.

disputes_again_resolved.description: Of those, the ones the second dispute round settled (they are in disputes_resolved too).

rejected.description: The dropped values by reason; every reason is written, 0 included. unknown_ticket: under no ticket of this job and round (another job's, another round's, a shard the node was not given, or none). unreadable: no result at all, or not shaped as an honest node shapes one. version: another controller version than the server's. content: not what its task asked for (the ticket is one shard's and the index or URL another's, or at odds with the task's pipeline: output mode, MinHash parameters, blobs, byte cap, languages). surplus: more values under one ticket than are taken: in the dispute round more than three, of which none is taken and each that would have been is counted here; an answer beyond the ones a round opens for a package; two results for one shard in one answer.

pairs.description: One record per shard and round in which the shard came back more than once, the first round or the repair round, ordered by index (a shard's first round before its repair round): its first two results of that round in the order the platform handed them over.

round.description: The round the pair is of: first (a shard the platform picked for the run's sampling) or repair (a shard that went out again, on two machines because the run asked for sampling).

results.description: Present when more than two came back: more values than the round asked for (a machine spent the slot of another task on this ticket); the shard goes to the dispute round.

incomplete.description: Present and true when a side is no result (a node fault, a dropped value).

signatures.description: Present when compared: the sides made the same signatures, different ones, or none (the pipeline does not sign: nothing to compare).

differs.description: Present on a mismatch: the fields that differ.

dispute.description: Present and true when this pair sent the shard to the dispute round.

disputes.description: One record per shard whose copies disagreed, ordered by index.

first_copies.description: The results with a verdict the first round returned for the shard.

repair_copies.description: The results with a verdict the repair round returned for the shard; 0 for a shard the first round sent to the dispute round.

copies.description: The results with a verdict the dispute round returned for it; 0 when more than three values came back (none is taken) or the round did not run.

agreeing.description: The most of those that agree with one another; when resolved, the results the accepted one rests on (executions in the report).

outcome.description: How the dispute ended: in the second dispute round when it went out again (again). resolved: one result was returned by the most machines, two at least, without a tie, and it is the shard's. The others leave the shard Disputed in the report. no_majority: no result was returned by more copies than any other, and by two at least. too_few_copies: fewer than two copies came back with a verdict (the round did not run, or more than three values came back and none was taken). surplus_copies: the leading result does not lead by two machines once the values that may be one machine's second are left out; as many of them may be as the other shards of the round are short of their three, and no more than the slots of the round that brought nothing at all. A dispute round that ends too_few_copies or surplus_copies sends the shard out once more.

results.description: What came back in the dispute round, in the order the platform handed it over.

again.description: Present when the dispute round left the shard with too few copies or a lead that may be one machine's, and it went out once more on three machines: that round.

after.description: How the dispute round ended: why the shard went out again.

copies.description: The results with a verdict the second dispute round returned.

agreeing.description: The most of those that agree with one another.

results.description: What came back in the second dispute round, in the order the platform handed it over.

accepted.description: Present when resolved: the accepted result.

no_result.description: One record per shard that ended without a result, ordered by index.

reason.description: node_fault: a machine that held the shard returned it as a fault of its own. no_answer: nothing that was accepted came back for it (nothing at all, or only values that were dropped).

faults.description: The fault codes the nodes gave for the shard, each once.

sampling.description: What the run asked for in second executions and what came back of it in the first round. The platform picks the packages that run twice and does not say which, so the server counts: how many packages the rate comes to, how many came back with a second answer, how many shards had two results that were compared.

rate.description: The share of the packages the run asked to run on two machines (CorpusOptions.SamplingRate held to 0..1); null when the script did not hand the run's options to Corpus.Integrity.

state.description: The account in a word. not_asked: the run asked for no second execution. as_asked: as many packages came back twice as were asked for, and shards were compared. short: fewer packages came back twice than were asked for, so some of the checking did not happen. none: second executions were asked for and no shard was compared, so the checking did not happen (a pool of one machine ends here). unknown: rate is null.

packages.description: The task packages of the first round (a package is one shard in a job of up to 1,024 shards).

asked_twice.description: The packages the rate comes to by the platform's rule: rounded up, one at least when the rate is above 0; 0 when the rate is 0 or null.

answered_twice.description: The packages two answers or more came back for.

compared.description: The shards whose first two values of the first round were both results, and were compared (the summary's compared).

statement.description: The same account in a sentence of fixed words, with the numbers in it.

rounds.description: How each round's fan-out came back, counted before any answer is opened: an answer counts whatever it held (results, a fault of its node, nothing readable). A round that was not run has zeros.

first.description: The first round: every package once, and the ones the platform picked for the run's sampling a second time on another machine.

repair.description: The repair round: the shards the first round left without a result, on two machines when the run asked for sampling, on one otherwise.

dispute.description: The dispute round: the shards whose copies disagreed, on three machines.

dispute_again.description: The second dispute round: the disputes the dispute round left with too few copies, or with a lead that may be one machine's second answers, on three machines once more (no package under a script written for a controller before 0.9.0).

packages.description: The task packages that went out.

answers.description: The answers that came back under the round's tickets.

unanswered.description: The packages no answer came back for.

answered_once.description: The packages one answer came back for.

answered_twice.description: The packages two answers came back for.

answered_thrice.description: The packages three answers came back for.

answered_more.description: The packages more than three answers came back for.

fault.description: A node's fault, a fixed code: disk (a local file could not be written or read), disk_space (no room for the shard), network (the origin did not answer this node with the shard after every retry: no connection or answer head, a broken body, a 5xx or 429 that outlasted the retries, a 407, a public origin's name the node's resolver turned into an address that is not public), language_model (the model did not arrive or does not match its pin), pdf_sandbox (the PDF sandbox failed to run a document), pdf_backstop (a PDF ran into the wall-clock backstop with fuel left), upload (a product or the results could not be uploaded), memory (out of memory), internal (anything else inside the node), tasks (the task package did not arrive on the node, or arrived as other bytes than its reference names: every shard of that package).

kind.description: execution: a result with a verdict on the shard. fault: the node returned the shard unanswered. rejected: the value was dropped.

code.description: Present for a fault (its code) and for a rejected value (the reason).

controller.description: The controller version of an execution; empty otherwise.

verdict.description: The verdict of an execution; empty otherwise.

signatures_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the signatures blob as the side made it, kept or not; empty when it made none.
